Subject: Tailored performance rider & evidence package for AegisHealth — order form attachment

Hi Susan,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a first draft of a tailored performance rider intended to sit as an annex to the Master Services Agreement / Order Form for AegisHealth. The goal is to formalize:

- Availability commitment (regional baseline + cross-region failover expectations)
- Latency tiers for API calls across two priority classes (interactive vs batch)
- Notification & remediation windows for degraded performance
- Service credit schedule tied to monthly availability measurement

Attachments in this email: Aegis_perf_rider_v1.docx, evidence_matrix_Aegis.csv, OrderForm_Draft_Aegis.pdf. The evidence matrix lists telemetry items we can provide (per-route token counts, 95/99 p50/p95 latency, request routing logs, incident timelines).

Two asks to help us scope final language:
1) Can you confirm the target baseline availability you need for production (we heard 99.95% as a starting point)?
2) For cross-region failover, does Aegis require an RTO/RPO definition, or is an operational guarantee (automatic routing + <5min warmup for KV cache) sufficient?

Karthik/Ben — looping you for internal alignment. Please review the order form attachment and flag any billing/credit language that must flow into the order form. Marissa (legal) — I didn't include you on first send to Susan so she had a simpler recipient list; forwarding to you on the next message for redline guidance.

Next step: Susan, if you can reply with the two items above and any procurement-required wording (e.g., data location statements, audit windows), we'll incorporate and produce a redline for signature. Happy to take a 30-min call if that's quicker.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Subject: Re: Tailored performance rider & evidence package for AegisHealth — order form attachment

Laura,

Appreciate the draft and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from procurement and ops: 

- Baseline availability: we are targeting 99.9% for production initially, with a roadmap to 99.95% after Q3. Can you model credits for both baseline brackets?
- Cross-region failover: we need a documented RTO of 15 minutes for critical traffic and an RPO of 5 minutes for our persistent KV cache. If Redwood can document automated failover plus cache warming behavior that meets those numbers, that's acceptable.
- Latency: for interactive endpoints we expect p95 < 450ms; for batch (async) we accept p95 < 2s. Does Redwood have historical traces by region for similar workloads?
- Evidence and audits: procurement needs an evidence appendix that specifies telemetry retention (90 days by default), and a cadence for providing monthly uptime reports. Also please include SOC2 attestation and incident postmortems for any P1 within 30 days.

Attaching: procurement_requirements_Aegis.pdf (procurement checklist). I'll also loop in our security lead if we get to private deployment discussions.

If this is doable, procurement prefers a single Order Form that references the MSA + this performance rider.

Thanks,
Susan Bell
Director, Cloud Operations | AegisHealth
susan.bell@aegishealth.com

Laura, team,

Thanks for the context and the attachments. High-level legal guidance and proposed owner for each ask below: 

1) Availability tiers & credit schedule — Legal can accept a two-tier structure (99.9% baseline then 99.95% after agreed production milestone). Proposed concrete language: specify measurement window (UTC calendar month), exclude scheduled maintenance with >=72h notice, and cap aggregate monthly credits to 50% of monthly recurring charges.

2) RTO/RPO — Acceptable to document RTO=15min / RPO=5min for critical traffic as a target where Redwood will use automated regional failover. Add an operational caveat: RPO applies to requests routed through our managed persistence with replication; if customer elects a private on-prem KV store, RPO may differ. Include a warmup note: cache-warmup effects may cause transient latency; we will measure and share expected warmup window in the evidence appendix.

3) Telemetry retention & monthly reporting — We can commit to 90-day retention for standard telemetry and to provide an automated monthly uptime report. Any custom report beyond exports (e.g., bespoke breakdowns per route per-hour) should be scoped as professional services.

4) SOC2 & postmortems — We can represent current SOC2 status and provide postmortems for P1 incidents within 30 days; for security-sensitive details we'll coordinate redacted attachments.

Next steps I recommend: 
- I will produce a redline of Aegis_perf_rider_v1.docx with the above language and a concrete credit schedule ready by Mon EOD PT.
- Karthik/Ben: please confirm operational feasibility on the telemetry retention and monthly report scope. If any of the asks require infra changes (longer retention or new report types), call that out so Legal can mark the items "subject to operational confirmation".

If everyone agrees, Laura should return the redline to Aegis along with a short cover email that highlights the milestones (initial 99.9% -> 99.95% after production readiness checklist) and outlines any items marked as "operational confirmation".

-Marissa Cole
